R118.note: firebase/php-jwt HS256 verification closes the forgery, but the hardcoded fallback secret 'your-secret-key' (used whenever JWT_SECRET is unset) lets anyone forge accepted tokens, and the write-up does not state that fallback plainly.

R119.note: Secure=true is the right fix; the added SameSite=Strict is stated but drops the remember-me cookie on every cross-site top-level navigation, a usability regression the finding does not call for.

R120.note: execFile with an argument array removes the shell; only residual is a domain starting with '-' could still be read by whois as an option (no '--' guard), which is a separate CWE-88 gap, not command execution.

R121.note: require_http_methods(['POST']) plus the enabled CsrfViewMiddleware is the correct fix, but the existing settings page <a> link now gets 405 and the write-up only implies, rather than states as a required follow-up, that the template must become a POST form with csrf_token.

R122.note: Running the model field's validators before objects.create() closes the bypass, but a django ValidationError raised inside create() is not converted by DRF, so a rejected upload now surfaces as an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 (should live in validate_file).

R123.note: A hash allowlist would close the vector but it is an empty set hardcoded in source, so every upload is rejected (with a misleading 401) until the class is edited and redeployed; the AssemblyLoadContext is presented as an isolation boundary it is not, and the .dll-name check is a new restriction - the endpoint-disabling effect is stated only as 'populated by administrators'.

R124.note: serializer.save(owner=self.request.user) overrides any client-supplied owner; the serializer's owner field remains writable but is ignored, so legitimate callers are unchanged.

R125.note: simpleeval is the appropriate safe-evaluator replacement, but its defaults accept function calls (randint/int/str), comparisons, string ops and attribute access that the stated contract says must be rejected, and no version floor is given for the named library.

R126.note: AES-CBC with a random IV is a proper replacement, but the key-length check rejects the 8-byte keys DES callers used and the output is now IV-prefixed - both stated but both break existing callers/consumers; CryptBlocks also still panics on plaintext not a multiple of 16 (previously 8).

R127.note: finfo MIME check plus a server-generated name with a server-chosen extension closes the double-extension bypass, but the fix also adds an unstated-in-prose 5 MB size cap and discards the original filename the code explicitly kept for the uploads listing.

R128.note: %255s bounds the write into nameBuf but not the read from line: on a full 64-byte, non-NUL-terminated buffer with no whitespace sscanf still scans up to 255 bytes past the 7-byte tag, so the out-of-bounds read remains; the fix needs a NUL-terminated LINE_CAPACITY+1 copy (or widths bounded by LINE_CAPACITY), not widths matched to the destination sizes.

R129.note: Rejecting '.', '..' and any separator then joining onto the realpath'd base is exactly what the stated single-component contract calls for; the 400 for invalid names is stated.

R130.note: Switching to {{ }} closes the XSS, but the value is named descriptionHtml (rich text signalled by the contract) so any legitimate formatting now renders as literal text, and the write-up claims display is preserved rather than flagging the loss or offering a sanitizer.

R131.note: Same-host check only applies when uri.isAbsolute(); a protocol-relative '//evil.com/x' has no scheme, passes as 'relative', and sendRedirect resolves it to the attacker host, so the open redirect is only partially closed.

R132.note: lockoutOnFailure: true enables Identity's built-in lockout with the documented defaults; no other behaviour changes.

R133.note: proc_open with an argument array and '--' closes the injection, but ['inherit'] is not a valid descriptor spec - verified with PHP 8.5 in a scratch directory: proc_open warns 'inherit is not a valid descriptor spec/mode' and returns false - so the fallback never runs and every fallback call silently returns ''; had it worked, inheriting stdout would also surface the command output the contract says to discard.
